resources.string: Logs stay in memory and disappear when the app closes.
No website addresses — enough to investigate a connection failure afterwards.
Includes the address of every connection — that is your browsing history stored on the device.
\"%1$s\" will be deleted and cannot be restored.
Paste a link (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria2://, tuic://, wireguard://, awg://, sstp://, l2tp://), a WireGuard/AmneziaWG .conf, or a subscription URL.
All device traffic goes through the VPN. Pick a mode to set up exceptions or an app whitelist.
Works only when connected through sing-box (VLESS/VMess/Trojan/SS/Hysteria2/TUIC/WireGuard).
All IPs and domains are routed as usual. Pick a mode to set point exceptions or a whitelist.
All traffic goes through the proxy, as usual.
Selected countries directly, the rest through the proxy
Their IPs and sites bypass the VPN — faster for local services.
Selected countries through the proxy, the rest directly
Only their IPs and sites use the VPN — minimal proxy load.
The handshake is sent as usual.
ClientHello is split into several TLS records. Almost no speed loss — try this first.
ClientHello is cut into separate TCP packets with a pause between them. Connects slower; use if TLS records did not help.
DNS, GeoIP by country, fragmentation, MTU
Apps through the VPN / bypassing it
Pure Kotlin, no native .aar: PPP stack (LCP, MS-CHAPv2, IPCP), SSTP over TLS with crypto-binding, L2TP over UDP (no IPsec/ESP). Needs on-device testing.
Unavailable: GRE (IP protocol 47) needs raw sockets/root, and the stack was removed from Android 12/13. Alternatives: SSTP, L2TP, WireGuard.
Transport: XTLS Vision / WS / gRPC. Flow: xtls-rprx-vision. Engine: libXray.aar.
Protocols: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, TUIC v5. Engine: libbox.aar.

Plain WireGuard runs through sing-box (libbox.aar). AmneziaWG 1.0/1.5/2.0 uses its own engine, amneziawg-go.aar: Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1/S2/H1–H4 obfuscation and I1–I5 markers. .conf/uapi generation is ready.

Experimental engines. WDTT — WireGuard through a VK cloud TURN relay (libclient.so + VK sign-in). olcRTC — TCP over a WebRTC DataChannel (olcrtc.aar + tun2socks). Marked with a BETA badge in the interface.

Instead of sing-box — for its XTLS Vision implementation (separate process, sing-box stays as the bridge to the TUN). VLESS is verified on a real device; VMess/Trojan/SS and long-term stability are not yet.

If a connection attempt fails, the tunnel does not fall back to a direct connection — traffic is blocked until you disconnect the VPN manually. It does not protect against the system revoking the VPN (another VPN app, \"Disconnect\" in system settings) — for a full guarantee at OS level enable \"Block connections without VPN\" below.
Open Hydra and it brings the tunnel up to the last server, if VPN consent was granted earlier.
The tunnel comes up right after the phone reboots, without opening the app. Also needs previously granted VPN consent — a dialog cannot be shown from the background.
Connects/disconnects the last used server right from the quick settings panel, without opening the app.

The only way to guarantee traffic is blocked even if the app or service itself crashes, not just when a connection fails. Settings → Network → VPN → Hydra → gear → \"Always-on VPN\" + \"Block connections without VPN\".
Device resolver, unencrypted — queries bypass the tunnel
Doesn\'t look like a DNS address. Examples: 94.140.14.14, dns.example.com, https://dns.example.com/dns-query/token, tls://dns.example.com
Supported: IP, host (→ DoH), https://… (DoH, path and token allowed), tls://… (DoT), udp://…

IP databases for ~250 countries are built into the app (sing-box rule-sets from MetaCubeX/meta-rules-dat) and work offline. Works for both sing-box and Xray Core — sing-box owns routing in both cases.

Splits the handshake with the proxy server so DPI can\'t see the site name in a single packet. sing-box only, and only VLESS/VMess/Trojan with TLS — has no effect on Hysteria2/TUIC (QUIC) or with Xray Core enabled. Not tested on real servers.
Change only if some sites hang while loading but small requests work — a sign of large packets being lost. For SSTP/L2TP it never exceeds 1400.
None selected — the rule has no effect
Domain-based matching (not just IP) exists only for %1$s: the rest have no domain databases. Sites on foreign CDNs will be classified as \"not theirs\".
All servers, subscriptions and settings in a single JSON file. Note: keys and passwords are stored in plain text — keep the file like a password.
Replaces ALL current servers, subscriptions and settings with the file contents. The VPN must be disconnected.
All settings return to defaults (theme, DNS, routing, Kill Switch, split tunneling, etc.). Servers and subscriptions stay.
Current servers, subscriptions and settings will be replaced. This cannot be undone — save a current backup first if in doubt.
Servers and subscriptions stay, everything else returns to defaults.
Disconnect the VPN before restoring — otherwise the tunnel keeps the old settings
Settings reset. Servers and subscriptions were not touched.
Hydra %1$s — multi-protocol VPN client. License: GPL-3.0.
The interface language. Connection logs stay in Russian.
If the VPN is on, it reconnects automatically a moment after each change.
If the tunnel drops, Hydra retries automatically with growing pauses (2 s → 30 s, up to 10 attempts) and picks up as soon as a network returns. With Kill Switch on, traffic stays blocked meanwhile.
Point the camera at a QR code with a link, subscription or config
No QR code found. Try a sharper, closer photo or scan with the camera.
This is a full JSON config (sing-box/Xray). It is not supported yet — import a link or a subscription instead.
Could not recognize this as a server link, subscription or config.
The link is too long for a QR code — share it as text.
This protocol has no shareable link format.
The link contains the server keys or password. Send it only to people you trust.
Subscription \"%1$s\" and its %2$d server(s) will be deleted.
Sent to subscription panels as x-hwid. Panels with a device limit use it to count this phone.
Every core is on by default. A turned-off core does not start the tunnel; its servers are marked in the Servers list.
VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, TUIC v5, WireGuard. Stays running inside as the TUN bridge for Xray, olcRTC and OpenFlux even when off.
VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks with XTLS Vision / REALITY, in a separate process. Used for these protocols when preferred below or when sing-box is off.

Obfuscated WireGuard, all protocol generations: 1.0 (Jc/Jmin/Jmax, S1/S2, H1âH4), 1.5 (I1âI5), 2.0 (S3/S4, header ranges) and 3.x (header protection key, content padding, random trailers, timers). Core: amneziawg-go 3.1.
Our own PPP stack in Kotlin (LCP, MS-CHAPv2, IPCP): SSTP over TLS with crypto-binding, L2TP over UDP without IPsec.
TCP over WebRTC through video-call services (Jitsi, Telemost, WB Stream). Needs your own olcrtc server.
TCP tunnel through document and messenger services (Yandex, MAX, Mail.ru, Cups). Needs your own exit node.
